description:
`RepositoryImage::file_bytes` returns the same `None` for an absent path and for a directory occupying it, so every consumer silently treats a misplaced directory as "no file". A declaration or item source replaced by a directory then disappears from results instead of failing.

## Background

Captured reads of repository declaration sources (`gates.toml`, `rules.toml`, `invariants.toml`, item registries) go through `file_bytes`. Before captured reads, the per-file readers reported a non-regular occupant as an error. Two issues under the mutation-session epic recorded the silent behaviour as a stated deviation pending this fix.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The captured image distinguishes an absent path from a non-regular occupant, and `file_bytes` (or its replacement) reports a non-regular occupant as a typed error to every consumer.
- [hard] REQ-02: Every declaration and item source consumer surfaces that error; none treats a directory at a source path as an absent source.
- [hard] REQ-03: One test at the image layer owns the absent-versus-occupied distinction; consumers prove only that they propagate it.

## Notes

Symlinked sources stay unfollowed by capture (no-follow capability layer); this issue covers non-regular occupants only.
title: Captured reads report a non-regular occupant instead of treating it as absent
